_meta.note: General, publicly-known interview format/pattern notes per school, used to ground mock-interview questions when a student practices for a specific school (Software_Timeline.md item 22). These describe format and general themes only (alumni vs on-campus, evaluative vs informational, common focus areas), never fabricated specifics about what any individual interviewer asks. Seed set covers a subset of the schools already in src/data/school-deadlines.json; extend over time rather than treating this as exhaustive.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, optional but strongly encouraged when offered, evaluative
schools.notes: Conversational in tone; alumni interviewers report focusing on intellectual curiosity, how a student talks about what they've read/studied outside class, and genuine interest beyond the resume.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted (Yale Alumni Schools Committee), off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly described as a genuine two-way conversation; interviewers often ask what a student would contribute to residential college life and how they engage with people different from themselves.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Similar alumni-interview model to peer Ivies; commonly touches on academic interests and community involvement.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: Known for a conversational style; commonly asks about intellectual interests and specific reasons for Dartmouth's undergraduate focus.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Given the Core Curriculum, interviewers commonly ask about a student's relationship to reading/ideas broadly, not just their intended major.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted for some colleges within Cornell, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: Format varies notably by which of Cornell's constituent colleges a student applies to; commonly touches on why that specific college/program fits.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly asks about fit with a specific school within Penn (e.g. Wharton vs. College of Arts and Sciences) rather than Penn broadly.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Given Brown's open curriculum, interviewers commonly ask how a student would use the freedom to design their own course of study.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly conversational; interviewers report interest in intellectual vitality and how a student talks about a topic they're genuinely curious about.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted (Educational Council), off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly focuses on hands-on problem-solving experience and collaborative work, consistent with MIT's stated culture, not just raw academic stats.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly touches on both academic interests and extracurricular/community engagement given Duke's stated emphasis on both.

schools.format: On-campus or alumni-conducted (regional), evaluative, strongly recommended
schools.notes: Known for asking specifically about choice of school within Georgetown (e.g. School of Foreign Service vs. College) and genuine reasons for that specific program.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Given UChicago's identity around rigorous, discussion-based inquiry, interviewers commonly ask about a student's intellectual interests in depth, not just breadth.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly touches on specific program fit given Northwestern's multiple undergraduate schools.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly conversational, touching on both academic and community/extracurricular fit.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, offered based on availability, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly touches on community and values fit given Notre Dame's stated institutional character, alongside academic interests.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: Commonly conversational, covering academic interests and why Emory specifically.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: As a women's college, interviewers commonly ask genuinely why a single-sex education environment appeals to the student, not as a formality.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: Given Williams' tutorial-style small classes, interviewers commonly ask about comfort with close, discussion-heavy academic settings.

schools.format: Alumni-conducted, off-campus, evaluative
schools.notes: Given Amherst's open curriculum (no core requirements), interviewers commonly ask how a student would use that flexibility.

schools.format: Not typically offered as a formal evaluative interview for most applicants
schools.notes: USC does not broadly interview most applicants; if this comes up, treat it as an unusual case and confirm directly with admissions rather than assuming a standard format.

schools.format: Not typically offered as a formal evaluative interview for most applicants
schools.notes: NYU does not broadly interview most applicants; general interview practice (behavioral, why-this-school framing) is still useful, but shouldn't assume a specific real NYU interview format.
